title: Moderna Norovirus Vaccine Fails Interim Bar: Trial Extends Into Fourth Season - Tech Times

analysis.time: Published on 2026-07-31; Event occurred during Phase 3 interim analysis in Q2 2026, with trial spanning enrollment seasons from September 2024 onward.
analysis.location_and_population: Global trial population; Northern Hemisphere (US, Europe, Japan, Canada) and Southern Hemisphere enrollment; affected population includes approximately 25,000 participants.
analysis.event: Moderna's mRNA-1403 norovirus vaccine failed to meet pre-specified statistical threshold for early success at Phase 3 interim analysis, extending the trial into a fourth enrollment season; confirmed interim miss, not efficacy failure.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Shares fell ~7% on news; Q2 net loss of $782 million reported; no approved norovirus vaccine exists globally; trial faces case-accrual challenges due to uneven geographic and seasonal norovirus circulation.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Trial remains ongoing, blinded, and scientifically sound; Moderna adding additional cohort to generate more cases; FDA clinical hold lifted in May 2025 after single Guillain-Barré syndrome case investigation; definitive efficacy readout pending sufficient case accrual.

analysis.brief_en: Moderna's experimental mRNA norovirus vaccine, mRNA-1403, failed to meet early success criteria in a Phase 3 interim analysis, extending the trial into a fourth enrollment season. The interim miss does not indicate vaccine ineffectiveness but reflects statistical thresholds and ongoing case accrual challenges. The trial, spanning multiple seasons and continents, has faced difficulties due to norovirus's unpredictable epidemiology, including uneven geographic distribution and outbreak clustering. Despite robust immunogenicity data from earlier phases, the pathogen's nature complicates efficacy measurement. Moderna's shares dropped ~7% on the news, though financial results showed modest improvement. The trial continues with additional cohort enrollment, and a definitive efficacy readout is pending.

title: Cryo-EM study reveals dynamic structure of human norovirus

analysis.time: Published on 2026-08-04. Event date not specified in the evidence.
analysis.location_and_population: Global human population affected by norovirus, with specific focus on the GII.3 strain responsible for repeated regional outbreaks.
analysis.event: A research team successfully produced virus-like particles (VLPs) of the human norovirus GII.3 strain and determined their structures using cryo-electron microscopy, revealing two distinct conformational states (resting and rising) of the virus capsid.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Human norovirus is the leading cause of acute gastroenteritis worldwide, infecting 600–700 million people annually. No effective antiviral drugs are currently available. The study provides the first evidence that the human norovirus capsid is a dynamic molecular assembly capable of adopting multiple conformations.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study represents a significant advancement in understanding norovirus structure and dynamics. Future research will investigate environmental factors triggering structural transitions, confirm if similar changes occur in infectious virions, and explore development of antibodies or compounds to stabilize or inhibit these transitions. The findings are expected to contribute to next-generation vaccines and antiviral therapies.

analysis.brief_en: A groundbreaking cryo-EM study has revealed that the human norovirus capsid is not a rigid structure but a dynamic molecular assembly capable of adopting multiple conformations. Researchers successfully produced virus-like particles of the GII.3 strain, responsible for repeated outbreaks, and identified two distinct states: resting and rising. In the resting state, the protruding (P) domain is close to the shell domain, while in the rising state, it is elevated and rotated with greater flexibility. These conformational changes may play crucial roles in viral infectivity, receptor recognition, and immune evasion. The findings provide a foundation for developing next-generation vaccines and antiviral therapies against this globally significant pathogen, which infects 600-700 million people annually.

title: No early success for Moderna’s norovirus vaccine in phase 3 trial - cidrap.umn.edu

analysis.time: Published on August 3, 2026. Event date not specified in the evidence.
analysis.location_and_population: Global trial with participants aged 60 years and older (up to 20,000) and an additional 5,000 aged 18 to 59 from countries in both northern and southern hemispheres.
analysis.event: Moderna's phase 3 trial for its investigational mRNA norovirus vaccine candidate (mRNA-1403) did not meet statistical criteria for early success, but the trial will continue.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The trial aims to assess the vaccine's ability to protect against moderate to severe illness caused by norovirus. Norovirus is the leading cause of vomiting and diarrhea from acute gastroenteritis among Americans of all ages and causes 58% of all foodborne illnesses in the United States. An estimated 2,500 reported norovirus outbreaks occur in the United States each year.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The trial is ongoing and remains blinded as the company works toward enrolling an additional cohort. The study has faced a clinical hold over a single case of Guillan-Barre syndrome and challenges with recruiting patients. Additional patients are needed because there haven't been enough infections to adequately assess the efficacy of the vaccine.

analysis.brief_en: Moderna's phase 3 trial for its investigational mRNA norovirus vaccine candidate did not meet statistical criteria for early success, but the trial will continue. The trivalent vaccine, mRNA-1403, is being tested in a global study targeting up to 25,000 participants aged 18 and older to assess protection against moderate to severe norovirus illness. Despite challenges including a clinical hold due to a single Guillan-Barre syndrome case and recruitment difficulties, the company remains committed to the trial. Norovirus remains a significant public health concern, causing an estimated 2,500 outbreaks annually in the U.S. and accounting for 58% of foodborne illnesses. The trial's continuation underscores the ongoing effort to develop a vaccine against this highly contagious pathogen.

Public health advice emphasizes handwashing, avoiding alcohol gels, and staying home 48 hours after symptoms cease. UKHSA attributes the variability to pandemic impacts and stresses that while concerning, current levels remain within expected seasonal ranges.
